The name of the programming language Python actually comes from a British comedy show, not the snake! Its creator, Guido van Rossum (I think your text auto-corrected his name to "zero when a resume"!), chose the name back in December 1989. Here is the story behind it: The Inspiration: Guido was a big fan of the famous BBC comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus. The Reason: While working on creating the language, he was also reading the published scripts of the show. He wanted a name that was short, unique, and slightly mysterious. The Result: He decided to call it Python. So, even though the logo features snakes today, the language was originally named after a comedy troupe!
